readerSummary: Jamie is presented as a technical project manager and implementation lead whose operating structures are shaped by how people gather, influence a system, learn its forms, and continue it. The artistic lineage remains a concise explanation of the method rather than replacing the professional role.
rationale: The About threshold explicitly connects artistic, civic, technical, and social practice. Three distinct project continuities supply specific participation mechanisms and public-safe proof: community vocabulary becomes organizer publishing, hospitality becomes adaptable onboarding and recurrence, and collective listening becomes campaign infrastructure and recoverable memory. The candidate preserves the people, places, and collective agency that make these more than administrative outputs.

criteria.evidence: The homepage names Technical Project Manager - Product Operations & Implementation. About opens with that same role, then Systems people can inhabit connects Open House, WOWList, Sunday Dinner / 196, NYC Artist Coalition, and Knowledge Wiki Graphs.
WOWList, Sunday Dinner / 196, and NYC Artist Coalition / FairRentNYC traces are recorded below.

About asks how structure helps people recognize relationships, participate, remember, and continue. Project pages make these verbs concrete through collaboratively editable posts, resident-defined working conditions, and shared decision/source records.

Open House governance belongs to its participants; WOWList names Richard Caceres; the coalition disclaims solo policy causation; Sunday Dinner identifies co-organizing and community credit while withholding participant-level records.

projectContinuities.evidence: Calendars made with Sunday Dinner clarified the need; collaboratively editable natural-language posts and followable keyword communities let organizers use their own scene vocabulary; public support threads and independent organizer tutorials document ways to join, publish, follow, and maintain local calendars.
projectContinuities.boundary: Jamie and Richard Caceres are co-builders. The 35-city scale is tied to a July 2017 snapshot; the 2026 return is explicitly only a public threshold, not an operating community-calendar relaunch.

projectContinuities.evidence: Two labeled workflow reconstructions connect proposal review, a needs-oriented video call, space/equipment configuration, independent access, and continued support; invitations, responses, food and welcome, minimal documentation, and follow-up make the next gathering possible. The shared-map photograph restores embodied place without being used as a participant census.
projectContinuities.boundary: The specimens are reconstructions, not the protected letters or operating-sheet rows. Participant identities, access details, private histories, and artistic-outcome claims remain withheld. Public milestones preserve Julia Fredenburg's co-organizer credit.

projectContinuities.evidence: Listening meetings and priority ballots become run-of-show documents, call scripts, public events, practical sessions, hearings, and follow-through.
